## Comparing plasmid- and chromosomal-borne *metG* genes



### Download all BioSample replicons for the *metG*-encoding plasmids


```{bash, eval=FALSE}
mkdir ./3_data/chr_seqs

cat ./1_data/plsdb_metG.txt | while read ID
do
mkdir ./3_data/chr_seqs/$ID
BIOSAMPLE=`curl "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/elink.fcgi?dbfrom=nucleotide&amp;db=biosample&amp;id=${ID}" \
  | xmllint --xpath "//eLinkResult/LinkSet/LinkSetDb/Link/Id/text()" -`
curl "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/elink.fcgi?dbfrom=biosample&amp;db=nucleotide&amp;id=${BIOSAMPLE}" \
  | xml fo -D \
  | xml sel -T -t -v "//eLinkResult/LinkSet/LinkSetDb/Link/Id/text()" -n \
  > seqs.tmp
  cat seqs.tmp | while read seqid
  do
  curl "https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=nucleotide&amp;id=${seqid}&amp;rettype=fasta&amp;retmode=txt" > ./3_data/chr_seqs/${ID}/${seqid}.fasta
  done
done
```

Checked folder contents. There was some duplication of sequences, due to the presence of Genbank and Refseq links in on NCBI. Some sequences had a huge number of files: 

- CP016613: 2650 files. Mostly very short (contigs?). Four files with full genome lengths (starting 119). Removed the remainder to another directory. 
- OY725756: 178 files. Apparently harbouring ~90 plasmids? Likely incomplete assembly.
- OY725916: 184 files. Again, a likely incomplete assembly.
- OY725987: 103 files. Another likely incomplete assembly. 

Remove the RefSeq entries. Keep the fragmented genomes in for the moment, but interpret with care.

Annotate all files with bakta for consistency.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd 3_data

find chr_seqs -name "*.fasta" > chr_seqs_collected.txt

mkdir ./chr_annot
cat chr_seqs_collected.txt | while read SEQ
do
base="${SEQ%.*}"
locuscode=`basename $base`
bakta -v --threads 64 --db /pub60/jamesh/db \
  --complete \
  --skip-crispr \
  --locus-tag $locuscode \
  --skip-plot \
  --meta \
  --output ./MetG_chr_tmp \
  --keep-contig-headers $SEQ
cp ./MetG_chr_tmp/$locuscode.gff3 ./chr_annot/
cp ./MetG_chr_tmp/$locuscode.gbff ./chr_annot/
cp ./MetG_chr_tmp/$locuscode.ffn  ./chr_annot/
rm -rf ./MetG_chr_tmp
done
```

Extract the *metG* sequences as before. 

```{bash}
grep "[Mm]etG" ./chr_annot/*.gff3 > PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches.gff

cat PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches.gff | wc -l #544 sequences

awk -v FS=";" '{print $2}' PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches.gff \
  | sed 's/Name=//g' | sort | uniq

awk -v FS=";" '{print $1}' PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches.gff \
  | sed 's/.*ID=//g' > PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches.txt

cat ./chr_annot/*.ffn \
  | seqtk subseq -l 10000 - \
  PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches.txt \
  | awk '{print $1}' \
  | tr -d '\t' | tr -d ' ' \
  | tr '\n' '\t' | tr '>' '\n' \
  > PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches_na.tsv
```

Create a file to match sequence names with projects. This was done in the main directory, where the sequences were originally retrieved from NCBI into.

```{bash}
find ./chr_seqs -name "*.fasta" -exec grep -H "^>" {} \; \
  | sed $'s/:>/\t>/g' \
  > ./metG_chr_seqs_headers.txt

cat MetG_chr_seqs_headers.txt | wc -l #1481
```

In R, sort the table out. Look to see whether there is the word 'chromosome' or 'plasmid' in the sequence description, and if so, add a column indicating 'chr' or 'pla' accordingly. Add 'unk' if neither word is present. Note: most of these are chromosomal, since the chromosomal sequences are usually not labelled (instead labelled 'genome'). 

```{r}
seqids <- read.table("./3_data/metG_chr_seqs_headers.txt", header=FALSE, sep="\t", col.names=c("file","description")) %>%
  separate(file, sep="/", into=c(NA,NA,"project","fasta"), remove=FALSE) %>%
  mutate(pla_chr = ifelse(str_detect(description, "[Cc]hromosome"), "chr",
                   ifelse(str_detect(description, "[Pp]lasmid"), "pla","unk")),
         description = sub(".*? ", "", description),
         file_id = sub(".fasta", "", fasta)) %>%
  unique()

nrow(seqids) # 1481 rows
```

Pull this together with the 'PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches_na.tsv' file.

```{r}
seqs <- read.table("./3_data/PLSDB_chr_MetG_matches_na.tsv", header=FALSE, sep="\t",
                   col.names=c("name","na_sequence","blank")) %>%
  separate(name, into=c("file_id","bakta_cds"), sep="_")

seqs_with_id <- seqids %>% left_join(seqs, by="file_id") %>%
  select(project, file, file_id, description, pla_chr, bakta_cds, na_sequence)

write.table(seqs_with_id, file="./3_data/MetG_chr_seqs_reference.tsv",
           sep="\t", row.names=FALSE, quote=FALSE)
```

Then will want to check for each project how many it has of plasmids, chromosomes, unknowns, with metG genes on


```{r}
seqs_with_id %>% mutate(encodes_metg = ifelse(!is.na(bakta_cds), "Y", "N")) %>%
  group_by(project, file_id, pla_chr, encodes_metg) %>%
  summarise(counts = n()) %>%
  mutate(classif = paste(file_id, pla_chr, encodes_metg, sep=".")) %>%
  select()
  pivot_wider()
```
